# Scriptorium
The knowledge packaging and deployment layer for portable AI skills

## EduStation's real failure mode
- Not an engineering failure -- the agentic loop and tool dispatcher had substantially landed
- Stalled from governance-before-traction
- 18 enforcement rules, a 5-tier compliance engine, a fully vendored legal corpus
- All built before a single real pilot with real teachers ever ran

## The pivot
- Stop building a dedicated agent harness -- that layer is being commoditized industry-wide
- Build the layer nobody has actually solved: turning a real expert's tacit process into a portable, audited skill
- Every skill runs on whatever harness the consuming agent already has
- Scriptorium itself never calls an AI API

## Two disciplines, every skill
### Grounding over confidence
- A claim without a real citable source is a bug, not a style choice
- Refuses loudly rather than guessing a plausible-looking answer
### Deterministic-first
- Where a script can decide pass or fail, a script decides it
- Quality evaluation and security audit are always two separate gates

## The 9-step pipeline
- Research and elicit a real tacit process from a real source
- skill-creator builds the artifact
- Quality evaluation across at least two harnesses
- Security audit -- a separate stage, never merged with quality eval
- Scout and harvest existing prior art, license-compliance check
- Dedup and novelty check, then a registry entry

## What is in the registry today
- 63 skills: pipeline infrastructure, foundation tools, a Vietnamese legal specializer network
- A full audience-tier ladder: Teacher, Student, Parent, TA, Lecturer, Lifelong Learner
- A deterministic Light Design cluster for posters, brand identity, and logos
- slide-deck-composer -- the newest skill, clone-and-inject pptx generation from a real template

## Zero-noise delivery
- skill-exporter is not a zip utility -- it is a Knowledge Deployment Engine
- Resolves real dependencies, filters by license and security status
- Hands the consuming agent exactly the skills the task needs, nothing more
- Right person, right task, maximally lean
# One skill that runs well, audits clean, and gets real use beats ten unused skills in the registry

## What is next
A parked slide-deck cluster, now built -- and a roadmap that keeps growing the same way: elicited, tested, audited
